content: A bunion, also known as hallux valgus, is a structural deformity that can sometimes cause pain. It affects the bones and the joint located between the foot and the big toe. Specifically, a bunion is characterized by an enlargement of bone or tissue around the joint at the base of the big toe, which is medically referred to as the metatarsophalangeal joint. In this condition, the big toe may deviate inward toward the second toe, a phenomenon known as displacement. The surrounding tissues of the affected joint often become swollen and tender, contributing to discomfort. The term bunion is commonly used to describe the pathological bump that forms on the side of the great toe joint. This bump may consist of a swollen bursal sac and/or a bony deformity that develops at the mesophalangeal joint, where the first metatarsal bone and the hallux (big toe) meet. The medical terms hallux valgus or hallux abducto valgus are frequently used to describe this deformity. The term hallux refers to the great toe, while valgus describes the abnormal outward rotation of the great toe, which is a hallmark of bunion deformities. Additionally, abducto refers to the abnormal inward drifting or leaning of the great toe toward the second toe, another common feature associated with bunion disorders.
